title: Flush mounting plate, 50 mm square, four corner holes
prompt: A 50mm x 50mm x 2mm aluminum plate with four 5mm diameter holes, one near each corner, each hole center 10mm from both adjacent edges
massBasis: JSON has no comments, so this array IS the comment: the arithmetic behind expectedMassG. It is inert — server/state/request.mjs:54 normalizes against a whitelist and drops it; only expectedMassG is read, from the RAW file, at server/pipeline/run-job.mjs:103.
NOMINAL is design intent, not the shipped mesh: 50 x 50 x 2 = 5000 mm3; four 5 mm dia. through-holes = 4 x pi x 2.5^2 x 2 = 50pi = 157.0796 mm3; solid = 4842.9204 mm3.
4842.9204 mm3 x 2700 kg/m3 x 1e-6 = 13.075885 g. This reproduces the FN-008 first-principles hand calc (13.077 g).
BAND = nominal +/-1% = +/-0.130759 g -> 12.945 .. 13.207 g, rounded outward to 3 dp.

Centered on NOMINAL, deliberately not on the fixture. The replay mesh reads 13.078605 g, which is +0.0208% high because the holes are 32-segment polygons rather than true circles (measured deficit 0.12592 mm2 per hole, exactly pi*r^2 - (32/2)*r^2*sin(2pi/32)). Re-centering on the mesh would bury that discretization error in the middle of the band instead of spending tolerance on it honestly.

WHY 1%: it is 48x the shipped fixture's tessellation error and ~3x the error of an absurdly coarse 8-segment re-mesh (+0.32%), so re-tessellating the SAME geometry cannot flip the gate red. It still rejects every defect class that matters here: all four holes missing (+3.24%), 6 mm dia. holes instead of 5 mm (-1.44%), 2.05 mm thick instead of 2.00 (+2.5%), 51 mm square instead of 50 (+4%).

KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: exactly ONE missing hole out of four is +0.81% and lands INSIDE this band. Tightening to catch it would put the band edge within ~2.5x of coarse-remesh noise, trading a real false-negative for a likely false-positive.

Tighter than the live-lane sibling samples/requests/live-plate-52.json (+/-1.5%) on purpose: this replay path is deterministic, whereas live generation is not — FN-018 measured a 3.6% mass spread across five phrasings of one identical intent.
